name: ODYSSEY 04 · THE KING AND QUEEN OF SPARTA

rows.t: Yet for no man of them all do I grieve as for Odysseus, who labored at Troy beyond us all. His absence is sorrow to old Laertes, to steady Penelope, and to Telemachus, the child he left new-born in his hall.

x_odyssey.speaker: character.menelaus
x_odyssey.payload: Menelaus speaks of Odysseus and Telemachus hides his tears behind his cloak
x_odyssey.direction: the young guest draws his cloak across his eyes
x_odyssey.delivery: host moving from memory to recognition and shared grief
conceal: full recognition until required private evidence is supplied
reveal: Menelaus speaks of Odysseus and Telemachus hides his tears behind his cloak

rows.t: Menelaus, shall I speak what my eyes tell me? Never have I seen such likeness in man or woman — this must be Telemachus, the son Odysseus left a baby at home when for my shameless sake the Achaeans sailed to Troy.

x_odyssey.speaker: character.helen
x_odyssey.payload: Helen enters, recognizes Telemachus by resemblance, and names him aloud
x_odyssey.direction: enters like Artemis, stopping short before the guest
x_odyssey.delivery: radiant queen whose visual recognition is immediate, precise, and emotionally destabilizing
conceal: full recognition until required private evidence is supplied
reveal: Helen enters, recognizes Telemachus by resemblance, and names him aloud

rows.t: You see truly, lady — this is Odysseus's son, too modest to claim it. I know such grief myself: my brother Antilochus lies at Troy, whom I was born too late to know.

x_odyssey.payload: Pisistratus confirms the identity and recalls his own dead brother Antilochus
x_odyssey.direction: bows his head over the table

conceal: full recognition until required private evidence is supplied

rows.t: Enough — we shame the feast with weeping. Let us remember supper now; with dawn there will be time for all our tales, and tears enough to go with them.

rows.t: Hear one deed of that man of endurance. He scarred his own flesh with blows, threw a beggar's rags across his back, and walked through the gates of Troy — into the city of his enemies, looking like a slave.

x_odyssey.speaker: character.helen
x_odyssey.payload: She tells how Odysseus entered Troy disguised as a beaten slave

full recognition until required private evidence is supplied
reveal: She tells how Odysseus entered Troy disguised as a beaten slave

rows.t: I alone knew him through the rags.

reveal: Helen alone recognized and bathed him

rows.t: Only when I had sworn a great oath not to name him did he open to me the whole design of the Achaeans.

rows.t: True, wife — yet you tell only half. Hear the horse's tale from within: I crouched in that timber belly with the best of the Argives, and Odysseus held command of us all, when you came circling in the dark.

x_odyssey.payload: Menelaus answers with the story of the wooden horse

rows.t: Son of Atreus, royal Menelaus, I came for this alone: tell me plainly of my father Odysseus. Did you hear that he lives, or must I mourn him? Do not soften it out of pity — tell me what your own eyes have met.

x_odyssey.speaker: character.telemachus
x_odyssey.payload: Telemachus asks directly for news of Odysseus
x_odyssey.direction: sets down his cup, meeting the king's gaze
x_odyssey.delivery: derive from current embodied condition and relationship pressure
reveal: Telemachus asks directly for news of Odysseus

rows.t: The gods held me windbound off Egypt, on the isle of Pharos, till hunger gnawed my crews — until Eidothea, daughter of the sea's old man, pitied me and taught me how to seize her father Proteus and wring the truth from him.

x_odyssey.speaker: character.menelaus
x_odyssey.payload: Menelaus recounts being trapped in Egypt until Eidothea taught him to seize Proteus
x_odyssey.direction: begins the long tale, eyes going distant
x_odyssey.delivery: narrator and memory performer enduring disgust, concealment, and a prolonged supernatural grapple
reveal: Menelaus recounts being trapped in Egypt until Eidothea taught him to seize Proteus

rows.t: The stench of the seals nearly finished us before the struggle began.

x_odyssey.speaker: character.menelaus
x_odyssey.payload: He and three men hid beneath sealskins and grappled the Old Man of the Sea
x_odyssey.direction: crouches as beneath a sealskin, arms locking round an invisible wrestler
x_odyssey.delivery: narrator and memory performer enduring disgust, concealment, and a prolonged supernatural grapple
reveal: He and three men hid beneath sealskins and grappled the Old Man of the Sea

rows.t: Which of the gods taught you this trap, son of Atreus? What do you want of me?

x_odyssey.payload: Proteus changed into beasts, water, and a tree before yielding prophecy

x_odyssey.delivery: ancient sea prophet with stable underlying identity and rapid lion, serpent, leopard, boar, water, and tree variants
reveal: Proteus changed into beasts, water, and a tree before yielding prophecy

rows.t: One more I saw, shedding great tears on an island: Odysseus, held in the halls of the nymph Calypso, with no ship and no companions to carry him over the sea's broad back.

x_odyssey.speaker: character.proteus
x_odyssey.payload: He revealed that Odysseus lived, detained by Calypso on an island
x_odyssey.direction: fixes his sea-gray eyes on Menelaus
x_odyssey.delivery: ancient sea prophet with stable underlying identity and rapid lion, serpent, leopard, boar, water, and tree variants
reveal: He revealed that Odysseus lived, detained by Calypso on an island

rows.t: Stay with me a month, Telemachus, and I will send you off with horses and a shining chariot — or does your heart already pull you home?

x_odyssey.speaker: character.menelaus
x_odyssey.payload: Menelaus urges Telemachus to remain, but the prince asks to return quickly
x_odyssey.direction: lays a hand on the young man's shoulder
x_odyssey.delivery: lavish host adapting generosity to the recipient's homeland
reveal: Menelaus urges Telemachus to remain, but the prince asks to return quickly

rows.t: No horses, then, for rocky Ithaca — take this instead: a mixing bowl of wrought silver, its lip finished in gold, the work of Hephaestus himself.

x_odyssey.speaker: character.menelaus
x_odyssey.payload: The king exchanges the offered horses for a mixing bowl suited to rocky Ithaca
x_odyssey.direction: lifts the great bowl into his guest's hands
x_odyssey.delivery: lavish host adapting generosity to the recipient's homeland
reveal: The king exchanges the offered horses for a mixing bowl suited to rocky Ithaca

rows.t: And this gift from me, dear child — a robe my own hands wove. Let it lie in your mother's keeping until your wedding day, and let your bride wear the memory of Helen.

x_odyssey.speaker: character.helen
x_odyssey.payload: Helen gives Telemachus a robe for his future bride
x_odyssey.direction: lays the shining robe across his arms
x_odyssey.delivery: gift-giver and spontaneous omen-reader linking bird action to household return
reveal: Helen gives Telemachus a robe for his future bride

rows.t: As the chariot rolls from the gate an eagle sweeps by on the right, a white goose in its talons — and Helen cries out the sign: so shall Odysseus, long away, swoop home upon the feasters in his hall and take his payment.

x_odyssey.speaker: PERFORMER.NARRATOR
x_odyssey.payload: As the travelers depart, an eagle carrying a goose appears and Helen reads it as Odysseus's returning vengeance
x_odyssey.direction: traces the eagle's path across the sky
x_odyssey.delivery: frame the action without replacing character agency
reveal: As the travelers depart, an eagle carrying a goose appears and Helen reads it as Odysseus's returning vengeance

rows.t: Meanwhile in Ithaca, Noemon comes asking: Antinous, when does Telemachus return from Pylos with my ship? I have need of her myself.

x_odyssey.speaker: PERFORMER.NARRATOR
x_odyssey.payload: In Ithaca, Noemon asks Antinous when Telemachus will return his ship
x_odyssey.direction: as Noemon, approaching the lounging suitors
x_odyssey.delivery: frame the action without replacing character agency
reveal: In Ithaca, Noemon asks Antinous when Telemachus will return his ship

rows.t: The suitors' laughter dies in their throats — the boy is truly gone, sailed clean under their noses, and the thing they mocked as impossible is fact.

x_odyssey.speaker: PERFORMER.NARRATOR
x_odyssey.payload: The suitors discover that the voyage truly occurred without their knowledge
x_odyssey.direction: marks the fear moving through the hall
x_odyssey.delivery: frame the action without replacing character agency
reveal: The suitors discover that the voyage truly occurred without their knowledge

rows.t: Give me a fast ship and twenty men — he shall have a black welcome home.

x_odyssey.speaker: character.antinous
x_odyssey.payload: Antinous selects a crew and sails to the strait between Ithaca and Same to ambush the prince
x_odyssey.direction: musters his crew and sails for the strait between Ithaca and Same
x_odyssey.delivery: humiliated plotter converting surprise into a lethal maritime plan
reveal: Antinous selects a crew and sails to the strait between Ithaca and Same to ambush the prince

rows.t: Queen, forgive the word I carry: the suitors plot to cut Telemachus down at sea as he sails home. I heard them lay the ambush with my own ears.

x_odyssey.speaker: character.medon
x_odyssey.payload: Medon overhears and tells Penelope
x_odyssey.direction: comes to Penelope in haste, voice low
x_odyssey.delivery: herald risking himself to disclose the conspiracy
reveal: Medon overhears and tells Penelope

rows.t: My queen —

x_odyssey.speaker: character.medon
x_odyssey.payload: she collapses in fear
x_odyssey.direction: catches her as her knees give way on the threshold
x_odyssey.delivery: herald risking himself to disclose the conspiracy
reveal: she collapses in fear

rows.t: Sleep, Penelope. Take heart: your son comes home, and a guide goes with him such as men pray to stand beside them.

x_odyssey.payload: Athena sends a phantom in the shape of Iphthime to reassure the sleeping queen
